<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 650" width="700" height="650">
  <!-- White Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Math style font definition -->
  <style>
    text {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 16px;
      fill: #000000;
    }
    .angle-text {
      font-size: 14px;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- Circle with center O -->
  <!-- Center O at (320, 320), Radius R = 150 -->
  <circle cx="320" cy="320" r="150" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <circle cx="320" cy="320" r="2.5" fill="#000000" />

  <!-- 
    Points on circle (Angles relative to center (320, 320)):
    O = (320, 320)
    Let's place points to respect general geometry and layout:
    - B near top: angle ~ -85° -> (333, 171)
    - A upper left: angle ~ -135° -> (214, 214)
    - D on left: angle ~ -175° -> (170, 307)
    - C near bottom: angle ~ -25° -> (456, 257) - wait, C needs to be lower right/bottom.
    Let's carefully compute standard coordinates (cx + R*cos(a), cy + R*sin(a)):
    
    Let's choose exact angles in degrees:
    OAB = 62° -> OA, OB, AB chords.
    Let's place B at -80°: (320 + 150*cos(-80°), 320 + 150*sin(-80°)) = (346, 172)
    Let's place A at -145°: (320 + 150*cos(-145°), 320 + 150*sin(-145°)) = (197, 234)
    Let's place D at -195°: (320 + 150*cos(-195°), 320 + 150*sin(-195°)) = (175, 381)
    Let's place E at -35°: (320 + 150*cos(-35°), 320 + 150*sin(-35°)) = (443, 234)
    Let's place C at -15°: (320 + 150*cos(-15°), 320 + 150*sin(-15°)) = (465, 381) -> Wait, C needs to be lower. Let's put C at -15°? No, let's make C at -10°: (468, 346).
    
    Let's refine coordinates so lines look clear and non-intersecting incorrectly:
    O = (320, 320)
    A = (180, 230)
    B = (340, 172)
    C = (450, 400)
    D = (170, 340)
    E = (430, 210)
    
    Let's check radii lengths to ensure they lie on circle r=150:
    Center = (320, 320)
    A: dx = -120, dy = -90 -> dist = 150. Angle = 216.8°
    B: dx = 20, dy = -148 -> dist = 149.3. Let's use exact trig for points:
    
    Angles from center (0 = right, 90 = down):
    A: angle = 210° -> (320 + 150*cos(210°), 320 + 150*sin(210°)) = (320 - 129.9, 320 - 75) = (190.1, 245)
    B: angle = 280° -> (320 + 150*cos(280°), 320 + 150*sin(280°)) = (320 + 26.0, 320 - 147.7) = (346.0, 172.3)
    C: angle = 30° -> (320 + 150*cos(30°), 320 + 150*sin(30°)) = (320 + 129.9, 320 + 75) = (449.9, 395.0)
    D: angle = 175° -> (320 + 150*cos(175°), 320 + 150*sin(175°)) = (320 - 149.4, 320 + 13.1) = (170.6, 333.1)
    E: angle = 340° -> (320 + 150*cos(340°), 320 + 150*sin(340°)) = (320 + 140.9, 320 - 51.3) = (460.9, 268.7)
    
    Let's re-verify positions visually:
    A: (190, 245) - upper left
    B: (346, 172) - top / upper right
    C: (450, 395) - lower right
    D: (171, 333) - left
    E: (461, 269) - right
  -->

  <!-- Tangents and point I and H -->
  <!-- 
    Tangent at B (346, 172):
    Radius OB vector from O(320,320) to B(346,172) is (26, -147.7).
    Tangent direction is perpendicular: (147.7, 26).
    Tangent at C (450, 395):
    Radius OC vector from O(320,320) to C(450,395) is (130, 75).
    Tangent direction is perpendicular: (-75, 130).
    
    The tangents BI and CI meet at I.
    Let's find intersection of tangent at B and tangent at C:
    Line B: (346, 172) + t * (147.7, 26)
    Line C: (450, 395) + s * (-75, 130)
    Let's solve for I or just place I nicely to the right:
    I = (580, 270) (approximate visual position that looks right and clean)
    Let's check if tangent lines can be drawn cleanly to I(580, 270):
    BI line: from B(346, 172) to I(580, 270)
    CI line (which is segment from C to I, and H is on the other side of C): 
    From H, through C, to I.
    H is on the tangent at C, on the other side of C from I.
    So H is past C away from I.
    Let's define I = (590, 290).
  -->

  <!-- Coordinate definitions (Exact for plotting): -->
  <!-- 
    O = (320, 320)
    A = (190, 245)
    B = (346, 172)
    C = (450, 395)
    D = (171, 333)
    E = (461, 269)
    I = (590, 300)
    
    Let's check intersection of BC and AE for G:
    B = (346, 172), C = (450, 395) -> line BC
    A = (190, 245), E = (461, 269) -> line AE
    Let's compute G approximately:
    BC goes from (346,172) to (450,395). Vector = (104, 223).
    AE goes from (190,245) to (461,269). Vector = (271, 24).
    Intersection G is around (380, 252).
  -->

  <!-- DRAWING OBJECTS -->

  <!-- Radii: OA, OB, OC -->
  <line x1="320" y1="320" x2="190" y2="245" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="320" y1="320" x2="346" y2="172" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="320" y1="320" x2="450" y2="395" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />

  <!-- Chords: AB, BC, AD, DC, CE -->
  <line x1="190" y1="245" x2="346" y2="172" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="346" y1="172" x2="450" y2="395" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="171" y1="333" x2="190" y2="245" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="171" y1="333" x2="450" y2="395" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <line x1="450" y1="395" x2="461" y2="269" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />

  <!-- Line AE (extended through G to E) -->
  <line x1="190" y1="245" x2="461" y2="269" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />

  <!-- Line OI -->
  <line x1="320" y1="320" x2="590" y2="300" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="5,3" />

  <!-- Tangents BI and HI (HI passes through C, with H on other side from I) -->
  <!-- Tangent from B(346,172) to I(590,300) -->
  <line x1="346" y1="172" x2="590" y2="300" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />
  <!-- Tangent line HI: from H(350, 480) through C(450,395) to I(590, 300) -->
  <!-- Let's calculate H: C is (450, 395), I is (590, 300). Vector CI = (140, -95). 
       Tangent at C is perpendicular to OC(130, 75), which is (-75, 130) normalized.
       Let's just draw from H(380, 440) through C(450, 395) to I(590, 300) -->
  <line x1="375" y1="444" x2="590" y2="300" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" />

  <!-- Intersection G (between BC and AE) -->
  <!-- Let's find exact intersection of segments (190,245)-(461,269) and (346,172)-(450,395) -->
  <!-- Using calculated G at approx (382, 252) -->

  <!-- Right angle markers for tangents at B and C -->
  <!-- At B: angle between OB and BI -->
  <!-- OB is (26, -147.7), BI is (244, 128) -->
  <polyline points="338,188 351,192 355,178" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1" />
  <!-- At C: angle between OC and CI -->
  <!-- OC is (130, 75), CI is (140, -95) -->
  <polyline points="438,382 444,369 458,375" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1" />

  <!-- LABELS FOR POINTS -->
  <text x="303" y="325">O</text>
  <text x="178" y="238">A</text>
  <text x="345" y="160">B</text>
  <text x="460" y="415">C</text>
  <text x="153" y="338">D</text>
  <text x="472" y="265">E</text>
  <text x="375" y="246">G</text>
  <text x="596" y="305">I</text>
  <text x="362" y="455">H</text>

  <!-- MARKED ANGLES -->
  <!-- ∠ABC = 76° -->
  <!-- Vertices: A(190,245), B(346,172), C(450,395) -->
  <text x="325" y="200" class="angle-text">76°</text>

  <!-- ∠OAB = 62° -->
  <!-- Vertices: O(320,320), A(190,245), B(346,172) -->
  <text x="220" y="235" class="angle-text">62°</text>

  <!-- ∠DAE = 70° -->
  <!-- Vertices: D(171,333), A(190,245), E(461,269) -->
  <text x="202" y="267" class="angle-text">70°</text>

</svg>
